thread:
leah: Heads-up -- CedarPort sent an RFI this morning. They've attached a vendor questionnaire and asked for a concise capability matrix, sample SSO SAML config, and a 21-30 day POC with a focus on data-at-rest controls + HSM import. They want per-hour burst pricing and a forecast for sustained QPS. Can we respond by EOW?

jamal: I can own the POC schedule and perf numbers. Need to know which model sizes they want (7B / 13B / 70B) and expected traffic pattern (spikes vs steady).

rick: I'll draft the SSO + network integration notes. We should include an example SAML metadata snippet and the required claims we expect (email, groups). Also add a note about SCIM provisioning being optional.

tay: I'll take the RFI security questions. Quick ask: do we confirm that customers can import keys into their HSM for Private deployments? If yes, what's the supported HSM list (Thales, AWS CloudHSM, YubiHSM)?

nina: Short answer: Private supports BYO-HSM via our import flow; Dedicated uses customer-managed KMS via provider integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). I'll pull exact supported models and the documented import steps.

jamal: For cost forecasting: propose two lines in the response: "sustained tier" (committed monthly QPS) and "burst tier" (on-demand hourly). I'll mock a TR cost example for 10k tokens/min steady and 50k token/min bursts.

leah: Good. The buyer also asked for evidence of log retention and audit trail (who accessed model weights, who exported keys). We should attach SOC2 + our audit log schema sample.

rick: For SAML sample I'll paste a minimal metadata example: ```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.cedarport.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.cedarport.example/sso"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

tay: In the questionnaire I flagged a couple of legal-risk items: (1) default backup key escrow wording; (2) data residency vs machine learning logs; (3) export controls on model artifacts. Legal suggested we propose a contract clause for backup key handling.

nina: I'll attach SOC2 + ISO certs and a short PDF with our audit log schema. Also adding a snippet showing the key import CLI for Private: ```bash
# example import into customer HSM zone
redwoodctl private import-key --hsm-type=cloudhsm --token=./import.token --key-label=cedarport-2026
```

jamal: Proposed POC timeline: Day 0 onboarding + SSO setup; Days 1-7 steady-state eval; Days 8-18 throughput tests (gradual ramp to N concurrent clients); Days 19-21 regression checks + final report. We'll offer a one-week extension if needed.

leah: Okay team, deliverables for EOW: capability matrix (compact table rows), SSO sample & SCIM notes, RFI annotated answers, POC cost workbook, certs & audit schema. I'll assemble into a ZIP for the buyer. Meeting to review Thursday 9:30am PT?

rick: 9:30am PT works. I'll upload the SAML and SCIM examples to the folder (drive link: https://drive.google.com/fake/cedarport-auth).

tay: Uploading annotated questionnaire now (link: https://drive.google.com/fake/cedarport-rfi). Note: I've put a red flag on the backup key escrow phrasing.

nina: Uploaded SOC2/ISO and audit schema (https://drive.google.com/fake/cedarport-certs). Also added supported HSM list: AWS CloudHSM, Thales Luna, and Fortanix.

jamal: I'll attach a preliminary cost sheet with both sustained and burst scenarios and a sample k6 script for ramp tests.

leah: Perfect. I'll consolidate and DM the buyer with the ZIP once we sign off after the Thursday sync. Thanks all :raised_hands:
